title: Implementing LGBTQ+ Inclusive Mental Health Care Into Practice: Barriers and Facilitators in an Australian Local Health Network.
abstract: Mapping implicit barriers to and facilitators of care in ways that are sensitive to LGBTQ+ people's needs within health systems is key to improving LGBTQ+ mental health care. We conducted such a mapping within an Australian local health network's mental health services ("the Network"). Ethnographic fieldwork (in which we captured researcher impressions of the service-sites and the views of staff), was analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. To help us more effectively evidence and target findings specific to actors within different levels of the Network, we further broke down themes and subthemes using the five domains of the i-PARIHS framework-, and the. Two primary themes were developed: 1) affective responses to the intended change, including, and; and 2) facilitators of pathways to change, including means of, and participants voicing. The findings suggest clear barriers to improving LGBTQ+ inclusivity alongside goodwill to support change. Our findings and novel usage of the i-PARIHS framework show promising applicability to other LGBTQ+ mental health-care equity settings.
